explain XXXXX in english without using word XXXXX?

i'm sorry if this is a stupid question, but i don't understand this phrase in english.
if XXXXX is an adjective, i know the answer. if it is a noun, i don't.
i've been trying to think it through, but i'm just so confused.

a:

in english we don't use that sort of notation for XXXXX when we have a noun.
the words in a sentence are more or less arbitrary. we can, and usually should, add the XXXXX to them in the case the noun already has the XXXXX in its name.
sometimes we do this by using the word XXXXX in the phrase XXXXX + noun in the verb.
like this:

the XXXXX 2001 is the greatest XXXXX ever!

we do this because the phrase above is ambiguous and has many interpretations.
